why_this_file_exists: S10 is the stage that drives Phase 4's deletion frontier to target. Seven of its nine rows are closed and asserted. Two are not, and neither is closeable as cleanup: one needs a vocabulary S7 was ruled to author and did not, and the other is not the duplication its name says it is. Writing that down as a dated, gated artifact rather than as commit-body prose is R-16's Shape rule -- prose is what the next baseline re-capture absorbs. A third entry is a pointer, not a defect: S9's open escalation named S10 in its for_the_phase_owner line, and this records exactly which half of it S10 closed and which half it may not.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves from defects[] to retired[] only when the contradiction is resolved in the tree, and only together with its gate test's own inversion: the reproducer stops reproducing and the test asserts the resolved property instead. Deleting an entry is not closing it.

defects.raised_by: the S10 lane, before its first src/ edit on the routing path
defects.what: Phase 4 criterion 9 has four clauses and two of them have no mechanism in the tree: the hardcoded first-defender scan still has occurrences, and no CcScope exists to resolve, so no Unreviewed scope resolves to SingleTarget on the pair defender and no disclosure naming the ability is emitted. `grep -rn 'CcScope' src/` returns two comments and no code.
defects.why: The scan lives in two places. `participant_timeline._first_pair_defender_id` walks `all_actors` for the first enemy (or answers 'main' for an enemy attacker) to rebuild the pair-enriched id of an applied self-heal copy, and the score path stamps `target` and `_event_id` onto the main's damage rows from `context.main_pair_params[0][0].participant_id`. Both encode one convention: the support scan runs against pair zero. Imperial Mandate's Command mark rides that convention -- the mark's subject is the CC trigger's `target_id`, which is whatever the scanned pair stamped -- so which enemy a cone stun marks is decided by roster order and by nothing else.
what_is_nevertheless_true: `program/route.py` already declares the two policies the fix needs -- `PairDefender` ('the single defender of the pair fight this event was priced in', named in its own docstring as the fail-closed answer for an unreviewed crowd-control scope) and `TriggerTarget` ('the policy that replaces the first-defender scan') -- and `resolve_route` is total over the ten-member union.
`program/build.pair_program` routes every authored pair damage event with `PairDefender()`, so the logical layer's half of the fix is landed and inert.

Phase 0 carries the sentinel that fires when the convention changes: `tests/test_phase0_sentinels.py::TestCommandMarksOneEnemy` asserts one authored immobilize marks exactly one of three enemies and that reversing the roster moves the mark, and its failure message says to read the umbrella's H2 row before pinning whatever replaced it.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: The umbrella records H2 as *deferred, default shipped*, and the shipped default is a positive construction, not an absence: `CcScope.Unreviewed` resolving to `SingleTarget` on the pair defender **with a disclosure naming the ability**. Authoring that vocabulary beside `cc_kind`, routing the Command packet by scope, and emitting the disclosure is the content of Phase 4's S7 routing bullet -- a semantic stage with an authored payload field, a coupled-golden footprint and its own Expected qualifying occurrences line. S10 is the cleanup stage and declares 0 occurrences by definition (phase criterion 8). Renaming the scan to `_scanned_pair_defender` and calling the row closed would put a routing decision behind a rename, which is this campaign's own failure shape: the convention would be exactly as positional afterwards, and one fewer name would say so.
defects.for_the_phase_owner: Either the phase schedules the shipped H2 default as its own semantic slice after S10 -- CcScope authored, the Command mark routed to TriggerTarget, the scan deleted, the disclosure published, with a declared occurrence count and an allowlist -- or the umbrella records that criterion 9's scan and CcScope clauses are deferred with H2 and restates the criterion. An implementation lane may choose neither.
defects.reproducer: `grep -rn 'CcScope' src/` finds only comments; `_first_pair_defender_id` is defined and called in `src/calculator/participant_timeline.py`; and `context.main_pair_params[0]` is read in the score path's support scan. An AST scan for a call to `_first_pair_defender_id` over `src/calculator` finds at least one.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: `CcScope` is a closed vocabulary in `src/`, `_first_pair_defender_id` has zero occurrences, no support scan indexes `main_pair_params[0]`, and a Command mark on an unreviewed scope carries a disclosure naming the ability that authored it.

defects.raised_by: S9's open escalation, whose for_the_phase_owner line named S10
defects.what: S9 escalated that every disposition every production path emits is MEASURED, and asked S10 to schedule the ledger join and the fold retyping or have the phase record a fixture-only discharge. S10 closed the half that was implementable as cleanup -- the *consumption* side -- and did not schedule the kernel-ledger join. The production side of the entry is unchanged and stays open in S9's own artifact.
defects.why: The consumption half was a live hole rather than an inert one. A WITHHELD leaf is absent from its payload by ruling, and `bis.part` built every fold operand as `Measured(value)` over `objective.get(path, 0.0)` -- so a withheld component would have folded as a zero no rule computed, into a total that then reported itself MEASURED. That is the incident at the aggregate, inside the surface D-72 exists to protect, and it needed no new producer to be wrong. `program/views.published_quantity` now rebuilds the operand from the payload's own entry, so the refusal propagates. What remains is that nothing constructs a `Withheld` to propagate: the walk still runs on `ScoreLedger`/`ReceiptLedger`, `OutcomeLedger` is constructed nowhere, and `AttackerOutcome`/`ObjectiveFold` carry plain floats.
what_is_nevertheless_true: Criterion 19's unit half is discharged: `Quantity.__add__` is tested over the full member x member matrix including the Starved-read raise.
Criterion 19's source assertion is discharged: every `.read()` on a quantity in `src/` is one of three declared sites, and only the algebra folds two of them into one expression.

Criterion 19's end-to-end backstop runs over a live roster receipt (`mandate_abyssal_curse_roster`) with one component withheld the ruled way, and its own R-05 red shows the same three parts folding to MEASURED(1540.0) when the absent leaf is read as a zero.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Unchanged from S9's entry: making a request emit a non-MEASURED leaf means running the walk on the outcome ledger and retyping the composition's folds from float to Quantity. That is a kernel-ledger change and a fold-type change, and S10 is the cleanup stage.
defects.for_the_phase_owner: The choice S9 put to the phase is still open and is now precisely bounded: the backstop fixture exists and is honest about injecting its withheld member, so what has to be decided is only whether the phase schedules the ledger join or records the fixture-only discharge in the umbrella.
defects.reproducer: Collect `{entry['disposition'] for entry in combat['dispositions'].values()}` from a live coupled receipt: the set is exactly `{'MEASURED'}`. Separately, `bis.part` reads its operand through `published_quantity`, so a payload entry saying WITHHELD makes the total refuse.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: at least one production payload carries a non-MEASURED entry, and the withheld-component fixture no longer has to inject one.

defects.raised_by: the S10 lane, closing an R-35 verifier's criterion-14 finding
defects.what: Phase 4 criterion 14 ends 'per-attacker totals are asserted bit-exact on the four bench scenarios against scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json'. The assertion exists and is gated (tests/test_golden_snapshot.py, repr(float) values, excluded from the 2-dp compare) -- but over the exact baseline's thirteen scenarios, and none of them is one of the four bench scenarios the sentence names (cassiopeia_3champ, cassiopeia_5champ, mundo_3champ, syndra_mandate_3champ).
defects.why: The two scenario sets answer two different questions and neither is wrong. The exact baseline's set is R-12's: derived from the damage_modifier producer set, covering both ledger shapes and one Catalyst roster, with the producer source read rather than typed so a seventh producer with no covering scenario fails. The bench set is R-07's and R-27's: four optimizer requests chosen to move the work counters and expose the compiled-to-receipt routing cost. A criterion that names one and cites the other was never dischargeable as written.
what_is_nevertheless_true: The bit-exactness property itself is gated, and more broadly than the sentence asks: thirteen scenarios rather than four, at repr(float) precision, with the exact file excluded from the 2-dp compare so the claim cannot be discharged by the rounded one (R-13).

The four bench scenarios are gated for equality of winner, score and every counter family by R-01 rows 8 and 11, on every commit -- what they are not gated for is per-attacker totals at full precision.

The divergence is bounded and measurable: `scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json`'s scenario set is exactly COUPLED_SCENARIOS' names, and the intersection with bench_coupled_optimizer.SCENARIOS is empty. The gate test below asserts both, so the row cannot drift into vagueness.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Closing it means capturing the four bench rosters into scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json. That file is one of R-32's five baselines -- 'golden_baseline.json, golden_coupled_baseline.json, golden_coupled_exact.json, campaign-fingerprints.json and item-coverage-classification.json move in their own commits, authored by the integration agent' -- and the lane's carve-out covers wall{stage}, alloc{scenario} and demonstrated_red{gate} and nothing else. Capturing it here would also move campaign-fingerprints.json's coupled_golden_exact counts, a second baseline in the same commit. The alternative -- rewriting the criterion to name the thirteen scenarios the instrument holds -- is a lane editing a success criterion to match what it could reach, which is the move this campaign exists to stop.
defects.for_the_phase_owner: Either the integration agent extends COUPLED_SCENARIOS with the four bench rosters and re-captures both coupled baselines and the fingerprints counts in its own commit, after which the criterion reads exactly as written; or the umbrella records that criterion 14's bit-exactness clause is discharged over R-12's derived scenario set rather than over the bench set, with the reason above. An implementation lane may choose neither.
defects.reproducer: Load scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json: its coupled_scenarios keys are COUPLED_SCENARIOS' names, and their intersection with scripts/bench_coupled_optimizer.SCENARIOS is empty.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: every name in bench_coupled_optimizer.SCENARIOS is a key of golden_coupled_exact.json's coupled_scenarios block, or the umbrella records the clause as discharged over the derived set.

retired.raised_by: the S10 lane, measuring the row before editing it
retired.what: Phase 4's deletion frontier names "WalkCompiler's duplicated dict/tuple branches" and criterion 2 says they are gone. `program/compile.WalkCompiler.add_engine_result` still carries a tuple-row branch and a dict-row branch, so the row is open. What the measurement says is that the two branches are no longer duplicated *constructors* and never were duplicated *logic*.
retired.why: Both branches end in one call to `compiled_damage_action` with one argument list, so S4's one-constructor move already collapsed the construction the frontier row was written about; `grep` for `SurvivalAction(` outside `program/compile.py` returns the one declared survivor. What differs between them is not spelling: the tuple branch reads positional rows from the light ledger, has no `unrepresentable_damage_receipt` fail-closed check (the pipeline's projection guarantees those rows are heal-free and linkage-free), sets `unclassified_delivery = True` because a light row cannot say whether a packet was an attack or a spell, and returns before the self-heal loop entirely. The dict branch validates `sequence`, fails closed on unrepresentable transitions, builds the trigger-linkage index and runs the heals. Two readers of two row shapes, sharing one constructor.
what_is_nevertheless_true: Migration frontier counter 5 is at its target of 1 and `tests/test_program_structure.py` asserts every `SurvivalAction` construction expression outside `program/compile.py` is the declared survivor.

The tuple ledger is not dead code being kept alive: `ledger_projection` selects it for score-only requests whose adequacy conditions hold, and it is the representation the residual counter (R-25) is most sensitive to.
retired.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Unifying the two readers means normalising a light row into the dict branch's named locals per row, in the loop whose own comment says it builds tens of thousands of sort keys per request, and then either giving the light rows a fail-closed check they cannot answer or moving that check somewhere the projection already decided it was unnecessary. The cost lands on R-28's wall ratchet and the only instrument that could tell a successful unification from a slow one is the bench -- so the change is performance-bearing by construction, which is not what a stage the table labels `cleanup` may contain. Deleting the tuple branch instead would delete the light ledger, which is a pipeline change nobody budgeted.
retired.for_the_phase_owner: Either the phase schedules the row as its own stage with a wall baseline and an allocation reading, or it restates the frontier row as what S4 actually closed -- the duplicated constructor -- and records that two row readers survive with the reason above. An implementation lane may choose neither.
retired.reproducer: `program/compile.WalkCompiler.add_engine_result` contains a branch guarded by `result.get("damage_events_tuple")` that returns before the module's heal loop, and a second loop over `result.get("damage_events", [])` after it; both call `compiled_damage_action`.
retired.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: `add_engine_result` reads one row shape, or the frontier row names the constructor rather than the branches.
retired.retired_by: The S10 lane, after an R-35 verifier reported phase criterion 2 NOT DISCHARGED on this clause. The escalation offered the phase owner two exits and an implementation lane could pick neither -- but it named a third the lane could take without either: measure the unification instead of arguing about it. Measured, it costs nothing the ratchet can see, so the row closes on evidence rather than on a restatement.
retired.how_it_closed: `add_engine_result` now reads both row shapes in ONE loop. The two readers were never duplicated *logic*, which is what the entry said -- but they were fifty duplicated *lines* of tail apiece, and that tail is now written once. What survives is a two-arm read of the two representations, in the one place they differ: a light row spells its time at `row[0][0]` and a dict row at `row['time']`. Each of the four differences the entry listed is preserved exactly and named at the line that preserves it: the light shape skips `unrepresentable_damage_receipt` (the fields it reads are the enrichment a light row omits, and `ledger_projection` selects that shape only where the adequacy conditions already exclude what the check catches); it sets `unclassified_delivery`; its `basic_attack` is False so only the explicit auto stream triggers Thorns; and it reaches the heal loop as a proven no-op rather than by an early return, because `pipeline.py` sets `self_healing_events = []` on the same three lines that set `damage_events_tuple`.
retired.what_the_lane_measured: The reason the entry gave for refusing was performance, and performance is measurable. R-01 row 8 on all four bench scenarios: every counter family, every residual, every winner and every score identical to S10's declared values (cassiopeia_5champ 1033/1015/967/3118, residual 19, score 5010.8, rungs compiled 836 / receipt_walk_candidate 131). R-01 row 11 (`--no-compiled`) exits 0 with an empty `routing_divergences`. Wall best-of-3 isolated on cassiopeia_5champ is 3834.6 ms against this stage's declared baseline of 3778.7 ms and its ceiling of 4156.6 ms -- 1.5% over the baseline, and the verifier independently measured 3827.5 ms on the parent tree, so the unification's own share is 0.2%, which is repeat noise. Golden is byte-identical and the coupled compare reports the same 145 allowlisted differences, path for path.
retired.gate_after_closure: tests/test_program_deletion_frontier.py::test_the_compiler_reads_its_two_row_shapes_in_one_loop -- one loop over the damage events, one call each to the constructor, the wound tuple and the live-amp lookup. Two loops show two of each, which is the inversion this entry's own rule requires.
